chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions, who said:
"When the woman prostrates, she gathers (her limbs), and when the man prostrates, he spreads (his limbs)."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: When the pray-er finishes eight rak'at of al-Zawal (midday) according to what we have explained, he should call the Adhan for Dhuhr until he says 'when he salutes, he should raise his hands towards his face'.
Thus its explanation has passed in its entirety, except for what he mentioned regarding the preference for reciting short surahs in the Dhuhr prayer, and that is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلزَّوَالِ: al-Zawal (the time of midday sun zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in prostration posture between men and women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the distinct physical etiquette (adab) of prostration, where women are instructed to gather their limbs to maintain modesty while men spread them, reflecting the broader Shia jurisprudence on gender-specific prayer postures. The text further contextualizes this within the procedural framework of the Dhuhr prayer, specifically addressing the transition after the eight voluntary rak'ahs of Zawal and the scholarly debate regarding the recitation of short surahs during this segment.
